svg.font-family: Inter, Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif
svg.text: an AI model that adjusts the process daily, treated as an Assembly — almost nothing here is new
AIControlUnit — a Control Unit Subclass, Not a New Branch
sits in a Point-to-Point or Star Assembly (Sub-model 3) exactly like a PLC would
— the AI just occupies the CU slot
no new topology, no new hierarchy level — an AIControlUnit is deployed exactly like any other Control Unit
On / Off — the Real State Machine, Not a Redrawn One
an Interlock forces exactly the Sub-model 4 transition it corresponds to — the target depends on where the AI currently is
Inhibited is unreachable from Off (Sub-model 4 has no such edge). So while the AI is Off, an
inhibit-type Interlock cannot target Inhibited — it targets Locked instead, via the same Off →
Locking → Locked edge lockType: lock already uses. Off never silently blocks Enabling and waits;
it actively locks out — this rule applies to every object with an Interlock, not only AIControlUnit.
leads to Inhibited (from Standby or On)
leads to Locked (from Standby, Inhibited — or directly from Off)
same highlighted paths as Sub-model 5 — this diagram is transplanted, not redrawn, so it cannot drift out of sync
operatingBounds — Required on the Process, Optional on the Twin
unbounded is only safe where it can't cause real-world harm — a structural rule, not a promise
a real setpoint, a real consequence —
the bound itself may turn out to be wrong — but that's a human decision (Sub-model 15), never a silent auto-widen
